packets.title: Matt Clifford standalone institutional story — first source freeze
observations: Clifford held a sequence of public-facing roles spanning AI policy review, international summit preparation, advisory implementation and ARIA governance.
The AI Opportunities Action Plan terms assigned him leadership of plan development while civil servants supported the work and officials were tasked with conflict identification.
The 2025 adviser role was unpaid and formally advisory, with direct reporting to the Prime Minister and DSIT Secretary of State.
Declared-interest and mitigation records establish a public/private boundary mechanism but do not reveal every decision-specific recusal or influence path.
supports: actor-specific institutional translation across venture, science, AI safety and public-strategy surfaces
need for decision-file and recusal-level acquisition
does_not_support: a direct Palantir or Anduril bridge
common purpose with Palantir and Anduril
packets.direct_voice_state: actor public statements and official role records; no affected-person voice is applicable to the actor chronology itself
counterevidence: the principal 2025 role is formally advisory and unpaid
official sources place final governmental authority outside Clifford
the source set does not identify a vendor-specific award or implementation decision authored by Clifford
packets.next_decisive_acquisition: One decision file connecting a Clifford recommendation to an accepted, rejected or modified policy instrument, including participants, drafts, conflicts, alternatives and implementation responsibility.
packets.falsifier: The acquired decision files show Clifford's role was ceremonial or convening-only and did not materially shape the bounded policy decision.
packets.stopping_rule: Do not promote beyond actor-specific translation without a dated decision file and observed institutional consequence.

packets.title: Palantir standalone institutional story — governance, ontology, deployment and exit
observations: Palantir's technical documentation defines an Ontology layer of objects, properties, links, action types, roles and permissions.
The 2025 filing documents a founder-control corporate constitution that is separate from customer authority inside deployments.
A local-government privacy notice identifies Palantir as processor and Foundry as the centralized Homes for Ukraine data platform.
MHCLG later built and operated Share in-house, migrated three years of operational data, exited the supplier contract and reported lower running costs and improved usability.
In NGC2, Palantir's Foundry is part of a named edge-to-cloud data mesh led by Anduril, with Raft holding additional registry, transformation and federation roles.
supports: a source-bounded standalone story spanning company governance, product architecture, public deployment, evidence custody and one completed public exit
formal distinction between customer data use, vendor platform role and founder corporate control
does_not_support: Palantir control over every customer objective or final decision
packets.direct_voice_state: local-authority user feedback exists for the Share replacement; represented guest voice over either platform remains unclosed
counterevidence: MHCLG demonstrated a completed in-house replacement in one bounded deployment
NGC2 assigns lead and complementary roles across Anduril, Palantir, Raft and public Army authorities
customer legal authority and configured permissions remain distinct from Palantir's corporate governance
packets.next_decisive_acquisition: One deployment-specific person chain and one enterprise-grade transition record showing data, schema, workflow, user, accreditation, residual custody and post-exit performance.
packets.falsifier: The proposed Palantir role in the bounded deployment is shown to be incidental, fully substitutable without material transition cost, or unrelated to the consequential decision.
packets.stopping_rule: Never import a company-level fact into a deployment without the exact entity, product, version, customer, user and consequence.

packets.title: Anduril standalone institutional story — public gates, integration, manufacturing and competition
observations: UK TALOS records show a progression from a £3.8 million trial to a £17 million Phase 3 contract for integrated force-protection experimentation.
The U.S. Army awarded Team Anduril a $99.6 million NGC2 prototype while explicitly preserving competition for additional team and component roles.
The Army later assigned Anduril lead responsibility for the NGC2 common data baseline, partnered with Palantir and Raft.
First-party reporting describes Lattice Mesh and Palantir Target Workbench in a live-fire training workflow; the performance claims require independent reconciliation.
DoD Title III funding links public industrial-base authority to an Anduril manufacturing expansion alongside private capital.
supports: a standalone history of public gates, prototype-to-delivery movement, integration responsibility and manufacturing support
does_not_support: successful performance of every product or claim
packets.direct_voice_state: soldier and official user descriptions exist in the broader program; target or affected-population voice remains absent
counterevidence: the Army funded an alternate divisional prototype and continues to solicit components
the public customer defines the mission and integration program
prototype, delivery and enterprise operation remain separate states
packets.next_decisive_acquisition: One accepted deployment decision file with requirements, evaluation, technical architecture, data and software rights, human authority, performance, unsuccessful alternatives and termination path.
packets.falsifier: The operating role is shown to be proposal-stage, customer-owned integration, marketing-only, or a replaceable component without demonstrated responsibility.
packets.stopping_rule: Keep proposal, award, prototype, acceptance, operational use, enterprise scale and effect as separate adjudicated states.

packets.title: Matt Clifford × Palantir — documented co-presence, no material bridge yet
observations: An official 2 June 2023 attendance list places Clifford and Palantir representative Louis Mosley at the same government AI roundtable.
The current source set identifies Clifford's public roles and the roundtable context but no bilateral instrument, decision, contract, investment, standard or deployment connecting them.
supports: a lawful acquisition target for meeting records, submissions, drafts and follow-on actions
packets.direct_voice_state: not applicable to co-presence; downstream affected-person consequences would require a separate deployment chain
counterevidence: the roundtable included a broad set of AI companies and government participants
Clifford's later formal roles were advisory and subject to disclosed-interest procedures
no exact material bridge is present in the frozen source registry
packets.next_decisive_acquisition: Agenda, minutes, submissions, bilateral correspondence, policy-draft changes, recusal records and any later instrument traceable to the 2 June 2023 roundtable.
packets.falsifier: No bilateral record or material follow-on action exists after complete lawful acquisition, leaving only broad-sector co-presence.
packets.stopping_rule: Co-presence remains co-presence until a two-sided instrument and material consequence are acquired.

packets.title: Matt Clifford × Anduril — exact bridge not found in Sprint 01
observations: Clifford's official AI roles and Anduril's UK TALOS contracts occupy overlapping UK technology and public-capability terrain.
The frozen source registry contains no exact appointment, meeting, draft, procurement, investment, award or deployment instrument joining Clifford and Anduril.
supports: separation of thematic alignment from an actor-specific bridge
packets.direct_voice_state: not applicable until an exact deployment or decision bridge is found
counterevidence: TALOS contract records identify Strategic Command and jHub, not Clifford
Clifford's AI Opportunities role postdates the first two TALOS phases
shared public-policy environment is an ordinary alternative explanation
packets.next_decisive_acquisition: UK ministerial and official meeting calendars, procurement conflict records, policy submissions, event rosters, correspondence and Anduril UK engagement records covering Clifford's dated public roles.
packets.falsifier: Complete two-sided acquisition finds no exact bridge beyond thematic or institutional adjacency.
packets.stopping_rule: Do not write a Clifford-Anduril arrow unless a dated instrument identifies both endpoints and a material mechanism.

packets.title: Palantir × Anduril — deployment-specific NGC2 integration with live alternatives
observations: The Army identifies Anduril as lead for the NGC2 common data baseline and Palantir as partner in an edge-to-cloud data mesh using Lattice and Foundry.
Anduril's first-party account describes a live-fire training workflow combining Lattice Mesh and Palantir Target Workbench.
The Army separately funded another divisional prototype, preserved flexible vendor teams and organized a multi-company Right to Integrate program.
supports: functional differentiation inside a public-customer program
packets.direct_voice_state: soldier-user operation is documented at program level; target and affected-population voice remains absent
counterevidence: Raft and other vendors hold defined roles
the Army remains mission author, customer and integration sovereign
first-party performance claims require independent acceptance and after-action records
packets.next_decisive_acquisition: Accepted architecture, interface control documents, data lineage, responsibility matrix, human authority, test reports, competing implementation results, software and data rights, and transition outcomes.
packets.falsifier: The apparent integration is merely co-presence or customer-directed interoperability without shared operative interfaces, responsibilities or accepted use.
packets.stopping_rule: Local NGC2 integration cannot be generalized into cross-customer or system-wide common purpose.

triad_guardrail.proposition: The current record does not establish that Matt Clifford, Palantir and Anduril form one three-way common-purpose compact.
basis: the Clifford-Palantir record presently closes only co-presence
Palantir-Anduril integration is bounded to named Army programs with public mission authority and competing implementations
triad_guardrail.reopening_condition: Acquire a two-sided actor-specific Clifford bridge to each company plus common design, governance or decision records connecting the three to one bounded objective.
